extracted.intended_audience: Title IX coordinators, school and college administrators, institutional compliance officers, and other recipients of federal education funds responsible for Title IX grievance procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance on required elements and permissible flexibilities in recipients' Title IX grievance procedures (e.g., use of single-investigator model, presumption of non-responsibility, timeframes, impartiality, supportive measures, appeals). Focused on ensuring prompt, equitable, and bias-free processes at educational institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of single-investigator model
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may adopt a single-investigator model (one person investigating and making a determination) as an option; availability of the single-investigator model is intended to provide flexibility to recipients and is not prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department maintains that allowing a single-investigator model will not necessarily introduce more delay than a hearing model and that concerns about bias/conflict are addressed by other regulatory provisions (e.g., impartiality, training, timeframes). A recipient choosing this model must still meet all grievance-procedure requirements (promptness, equity, impartiality). Nothing precludes a postsecondary institution from using single-investigator only when both parties consent in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to articulate consistent principles when procedures apply to some complaints (§106.45(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a recipient adopts grievance procedures that apply to the resolution of some, but not all, complaints (for example, using a live hearing for some complaints and a single-investigator model for others), the recipient must articulate consistent principles for how it will determine which procedures apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievance procedures must explain the circumstances or types of complaints to which each model applies, and determinations must be made in a manner that treats complainants and respondents equitably, consistent with §106.45(b)(1). The Department added §106.45(b)(8) to ensure educational communities are aware in advance when a recipient will utilize a single-investigator model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal process parity (§106.45(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's appeal process must, at minimum, be the same as it offers in all other comparable proceedings, if any, including proceedings relating to other discrimination complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to require a live hearing during appeals but notes recipients may provide such a hearing in their discretion or when required by other law. Appeals must meet parity with comparable institutional proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and no conflicts for Title IX personnel (§106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person designated as a Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker must not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This impartiality requirement also applies to those facilitating informal resolution processes. These provisions are intended to ensure neutral, bias-free grievance processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training on impartiality and avoiding prejudgment (§106.8(d)(2)(iii) and (d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and employees involved in grievance procedures, informal resolution, or the provision of supportive measures must receive training on how to serve impartially, including by avoiding prejudgment of the facts at issue, conflicts of interest, and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is required and intended to operationalize the neutrality expectations in the regulations and to increase confidence in Title IX proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that the respondent is not responsible until a determination at conclusion (§106.45(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations maintain the presumption that the respondent is not responsible for the alleged sex discrimination until a determination is made at the conclusion of the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption reinforces that the burden of proof is on the recipient (not on either party) and is intended to support neutral, bias-free proceedings. The Department clarifies this is not a presumption that a complainant is lying, nor is it a criminal-style presumption of 'innocent until proven guilty.' The presumption does not require importing criminal-law concepts such as the Fifth Amendment into school proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of burden of proof and result if evidence insufficient (§106.45(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden of proof in Title IX grievance procedures rests with the recipient; if responsibility is not established by the evidence in accordance with the applicable standard of proof, the recipient must find that the respondent is not responsible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allocation is consistent with civil/administrative proceedings; recipients must gather evidence and meet the chosen standard of proof before finding responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on drawing inferences from silence in certain postsecondary proceedings (§106.46(f)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: In sex-based harassment proceedings at postsecondary institutions involving a student complainant or student respondent, a decisionmaker must not draw an inference about whether sex-based harassment occurred based solely on a party's or witness's refusal to respond to questions deemed relevant and not impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to add a separate regulatory sentence that a respondent's silence must not be held against them because existing provisions (including this one) prevent such inferences; recipients also are not required to import criminal protections into disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures: neutral, non-punitive, and challengeable (§106.44(g)(2) and (g)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures may be provided to a complainant or respondent so long as such measures are not unreasonably burdensome, are not provided for punitive or disciplinary reasons, and are designed to protect safety or provide support during grievance or informal resolution processes; parties must be given timely opportunity to challenge the provision of supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department removed language that suggested supportive measures could be 'temporary measures that burden a respondent' to avoid implying unequal treatment. Supportive measures must be implemented neutrally and allow parties an opportunity to challenge them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to establish reasonably prompt timeframes for major stages (§106.45(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must establish reasonably prompt timeframes for the major stages of the grievance procedures (examples include evaluation, investigation, determination, and appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeframes should balance prompt resolution with thorough, accurate investigations and may include additional stages at a recipient's discretion. The Department declined to set a fixed 60-day requirement but recognizes recipients may adopt 60 days if they deem it reasonable. Recipients decide whether to use business or calendar days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions for good cause and notice requirement (§106.46(e)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any extensions of established timeframes must be reasonable and for good cause; recipients must notify the parties of the reason for the extension, and §106.46(e)(5) requires providing 'reasonable extension[s] of timeframes on a case-by-case basis for good cause with written notice to the parties that includes the reason for the delay.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulations prohibit indefinite delays and require transparency about timeframes and reasons for extensions. Recipients may define 'good cause' in their policies; parties must be informed in writing when extensions occur and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation stage is a major stage requiring a timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient's initial evaluation of whether to dismiss or investigate a complaint of sex discrimination constitutes a major stage of the grievance procedure and should have a timeframe specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For promptness and transparency, parties should be aware of the timeframe governing when the initial evaluation will be completed; recipients may set additional stages and timeframes as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: No statutory limitations requirement for filing complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to adopt a statute of limitations for filing a sex discrimination complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposing a filing deadline could be unfair to complainants who delay reporting for many reasons; recipients remain obligated to respond to known conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion to use outside entities, panels, multiple investigators, and to separate roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have discretion to use outside entities to conduct investigations; to employ a panel or board of individuals as the decisionmaker; to employ more than one investigator for a complaint; and to separate the roles of decisionmaker, investigator, and sanctioning officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such structural choices are permitted so long as the recipient's grievance procedures comport with the regulatory requirements (promptness, impartiality, equitable treatment, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to respond promptly and effectively upon knowledge (§106.44)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even in the absence of a complaint, if a recipient has knowledge of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, the recipient must respond promptly and effectively, including offering supportive measures and the option of informal resolution where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This duty ensures recipients take steps to prevent continuation or recurrence of sex discrimination and support affected parties during grievance or informal resolution processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to remove a respondent on an emergency basis (§106.44(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.44(h), recipients may remove a respondent on an emergency basis when appropriate without awaiting the conclusion of the grievance procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency removals are permitted to protect safety; such actions are separate from determinations of responsibility and are not punitive measures under the supportive measures provisions.
